subject: baku
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: baku, the dream-eating tapir spirit.
Style: ukiyo-e woodblock print.
reasoning:
I'm designing a baku creature blending tapir body, elephant trunk, tiger paws, ox tail, and lion mane, rendered in ukiyo-e style with flat indigo, vermilion, cream, and black outlines plus wave and cloud motifs. I want to keep the module efficient while planning the scale and SDK structure carefully to avoid errors.

Setting up the skeleton with hip, spine, chest, neck, head, legs, and tail, then defining the color palette and working out a seigaiha wave pattern paint function for the body's flank texture...

Still planning body geometry...

Narrowing the neck taper toward the head joint, then placing the head with a forward-down orientation to set up the tapir-like skull shape as a scaled sphere positioned slightly forward along the head's local axes.

Now I'm sweeping the trunk/snout as a curved path that starts near the muzzle and curls downward and up at the tip, with tapering radius and a cream-colored band near the tip to mimic a tapir's lip markings. I'm starting the jaw joint setup, parented to the head.

Jaw continuing: capsule rod for the lower jaw in cream, plus two small fang spikes. For the eyes, I'm placing decal-based ukiyo-e style eyes on the skull — slit pupil, white sclera, vermilion rim — positioned near the front-left of the skull surface with mirrored placement for symmetry.

Checking the math confirms the eye point sits close enough to the skull's ellipsoid surface. Now I'm designing round tapir-like ears with white rims, using an extruded octagon outline placed near the top-rear of the head, with a smaller cream inner layer for depth.

Thinking through the baku's traditional traits—elephant trunk, rhino eyes, ox tail, tiger paws—I want to add short ivory tusks near the trunk and a small flame-like mane in an ukiyo-e style to give it more character.

For decoration, I'm considering cloud-swirl motifs on the shoulders and hips rendered as SVG spiral decals, plus bold ink-style outlines using dark detailing and cel-shaded toon materials rather than attempting a geometry-based outline shell, which would be overly complex.

Now I'm setting up the tapir's legs—four short, thick limbs with hip/foot chains and bend joints, defining shoulder and foot target positions, parenting to spine joints, and working out the leg lengths so the front legs span from shoulder height down to the ground properly.

I'm adding sweep radii for the leg chains and sculpting flattened spheres for the paws, cream-colored with ink toe details attached to the tip joints.

For the belly and waves, I'm layering a cream countershade under a cel-shaded seigaiha pattern across the flanks, built from indigo with pale blue wave lines and ink accents. For the body colors, I'm leaning toward a tapir-inspired design with a deep indigo front and a cream saddle marking the rear, keying the pattern off the z-position.

Now I'm thinking through the coat split more carefully: cream with blue seigaiha waves on the hindquarters, indigo with white waves up front, separated by a wobbly boundary using a sine wave for a hand-painted feel. For the legs I'll reuse the same position-based coat paint so the pattern continues naturally, and I'm considering adding vermilion ankle cuffs as a stripe accent near the feet.

For the mane, I'm planning lion-like flame cards scattered along the neck and spine, using a flame-blade texture with a vermilion-to-gold gradient and ink outlines, swept back along the neck curve. For the tail, I'm chaining a few segments from the hips tapering to a tip, then adding a ring of flame-card spikes around the tip as a tuft.

Now I'm considering whether the trunk needs its own chain joint structure for rigging flexibility, parenting it to the head and defining its path points.

Building the trunk sweep with tapering radii and a color gradient from body tone to cream at the tip, plus a small ink nostril placed near the trunk's end.

For the tusks, I'm placing small ivory spike shapes near the trunk base on the upper jaw, computing positions and directions in local head coordinates so they curve outward symmetrically on each side.

Now I'm fleshing out head details: an indigo skull, ink brow ridges, cream cheeks, and a vermilion spiral decal on each cheek. I'm also placing a gold crescent-moon-and-tomoe emblem on the forehead using local head coordinates for position and direction, and considering but likely skipping small horns.

Moving on to ears, mane, and whiskers -- adding thin cream catmull-curve whiskers sweeping from the trunk base, two per side. For the eyes I'm drafting an ukiyo-e style decal: a heavy black-outlined almond shape with thick ink eyebrows, vermilion eyeshadow, dark iris, and a white glint. I'm also sketching gold-and-cream swirled "kumo" cloud decals to place symmetrically along the body's flanks.

I'm computing surface hit points so the cloud decals project correctly onto the body near the shoulder and rear on both sides, then adding a small glowing dream pearl gem on the forehead for a nice focal touch, while deciding to skip extra smoke wisps near the trunk. I'm also positioning the lower jaw joint beneath the trunk to match the tapir-like head structure.

Checking that head-relative local directions still work correctly regardless of head tilt, then assigning front legs to parent off the spine's last joint and hind legs to the hips. I'm now considering a chest accessory—a rope collar or gold bead necklace with a tassel—as an ukiyo-e-style decorative touch.

Adding the rope sweep at 0.014 thickness with 14 gold beads, then working out where to anchor the tassel cards by sampling the loop path at the bottom-front point opposite the top.

I'm resolving the ambiguity by using the nearest-surface lookup near the neck front, pushing forward and down slightly to find a hit point, then building a frame from that hit so the bone data carries through for the hanging cards. Now I'm sketching the tassel's gold knot texture.

For textures, I'm settling on six: eye, cloud, flame mane, emblem, tassel, and cheek swirl, with no separate ground needed. For the paws, I'm adding small toe spheres and ink claw spikes positioned off each leg's tip bone.

Part count seems reasonable overall, so now I'm adding brow ridges as ink sweeps curving over each eye in vermilion, anchored to the head bone. For the mane, I'm planning cards swept along the neck and back, scattered over surfaces facing upward to catch the right flow direction.

Now I'm sketching out the flame shapes themselves — scattering roughly 45 per mane region, filtered to the correct body zone, mixing vermilion and gold flame textures drawn as curved SVG paths with ink outlines, rooted at the base and tapering to a tip at top.

Writing wave tiling function...

Still refining the ring threshold logic, restricting it to the upper body normal so the effect doesn't wrap wrong. Now I'm defining the coat paint with a wavy boundary edge separating a cream/tan highlight region from an indigo/blue shadow region, blended with the wave color helper.

For non-paint parts I'll just use the cel paints directly since they share the same atlas as plain strings. Now I'm working out the body sweep geometry along the spine chain—varying radius per segment to make the rear fuller, rounding the rump with capped ends, and figuring out where the neck and hip sections should begin and end along the z-axis.

Still refining the leg placement and proportions against the body so the hip joints, leg roots, and shoulder heights line up believably with the belly clearance and reach distance to the feet.

Now I'm working out the neck and head geometry, placing two neck joints that curve upward and forward from the spine's end, then attaching the skull at the neck tip with its own forward offset so the overall body length and head height come out proportionate.

For ears, I'm defining their attachment at the head using local offsets outward and upward, with the ear plane oriented so its thickness runs along the forward axis and tilted slightly outward, then outlining each ear as a small ellipse-like shape.

Since these are tapir-style ears with pale tips, I'm layering a cream outer rim around a thicker indigo inner section, both anchored to the head bone, before moving on to add a cheek swirl decal on the skull offset to the side.

For the swirl I'm placing a vermilion spiral-with-ink-stroke texture angled outward on the cheek, then setting up a forehead emblem decal with a gold circle and crescent-moon motif, double-checking it lands within the ellipsoid bounds, and finally applying a moderate glow effect to the textured emblem.

Now I'm sweeping each whisker as a tapered curve from a point near the muzzle out to a tip offset sideways, downward, and forward using local coordinates with mirrored left/right signs, then moving on to plan the collar with rope, beads, and tassel, and scattering mane tufts across the neck surface.

For the body I'm scattering fur cards with a filter based on normal direction and position, then placing the tail tuft ring and starting on hooves and paw positions, beginning with the leg geometry that builds limb curves from hip to foot with a bend direction per side.

Placing the paw sphere so its bottom aligns with the foot y-position, adjusting foot height to 0.065 to keep the leg tube radius tucked in nicely without clipping through the ground.

Setting up the hind leg with hip, knee, and ankle joints, lengthening the segments slightly so the knee bends forward noticeably instead of staying nearly straight. Adding three small toe spheres with claw details to the paw tip, then finalizing the component export and writing the eye SVG.

Still refining the eyebrow curve, then I'm sketching a swirling cloud icon using overlapping circles with spiral strokes in cream and vermilion tones, and designing a gold emblem with a ring and crescent moon shape inside a 64x64 viewBox.

For the tassel element, I need to flip my approach—since the card is rotated 180 degrees, the attachment point should be drawn at the bottom of the shape with the hanging strands extending upward toward the top.

Now I'm sketching the rope as a swept path along the loop curve with a vermilion stroke, and scattering gold bead spheres evenly along that same loop using the path's frame data for positioning. I'm also finalizing my color constants, pulling the glow effect from the glow kit and the ink tone from the toon kit, then setting up the wave-paint function for the seigaiha pattern.

With the colors sorted, I'm defining the trunk's sweep with banded coloring that shifts from the trunk tone into cream near the tip, and mapping out joint naming across the spine, neck, tail, trunk, and leg chains to keep everything unique. I'm adding a jaw joint parented to the head with its own aim and role, building the lower jaw part so it peeks out beneath the trunk, and starting on small cream fang spikes jutting upward from it.

Now I'm setting up a tufted ring of flame-colored cards at the tail tip that flare outward with a tilt toward the tail's tangent direction, plus a small cream core sphere anchored to the last tail joint to cap it off. Then I'm moving into writing out the full body sweep along the spine chain.
